source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserve the singular high-priesthood construction with both names and the prophetic word-coming formula.
key_decisions.before: during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, God’s word came to John son of Zechariah in the wilderness.
key_decisions.after: During the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John, Zechariah's son, in the wilderness.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John son of Zechariah in the wilderness.

key_decisions.rationale: Retain geography and the linked repentance, baptism, and forgiveness without specifying a theological mechanism.
key_decisions.before: He went throughout the region around the Jordan, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins,
key_decisions.after: He went throughout the region around the Jordan, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he went into all the region around the Jordan, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins,

key_decisions.rationale: Keep crowds as the addressees rather than replace them with the leaders named in another Gospel.
key_decisions.before: John said to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him, “Offspring of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
key_decisions.after: John said to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him, “You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Therefore he was saying to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him, “Offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?

key_decisions.rationale: Keep the practical response and the question repeated by the next groups.
key_decisions.before: The crowds asked him, “What then should we do?”
key_decisions.after: The crowds asked him, “What, then, should we do?”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And the crowds were asking him, saying, “What then shall we do?”

key_decisions.rationale: Retain the exact two-to-none clothing comparison and corresponding food obligation.
key_decisions.before: He answered, “Whoever has two tunics must share with the one who has none, and whoever has food must do the same.”
key_decisions.after: He answered, “Anyone with two tunics should share with someone who has none. Anyone with food should do the same.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And answering, he said to them, “The one who has two tunics must share with the one who has none, and the one who has food must do likewise.”

key_decisions.rationale: Keep the named occupation and baptism purpose without generalizing them as sinners.
key_decisions.before: Tax collectors also came to be baptized and asked him, “Teacher, what should we do?”
key_decisions.after: Tax collectors also came to be baptized. “Teacher,” they asked, “what should we do?”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And tax collectors also came to be baptized, and they said to him, “Teacher, what shall we do?”

key_decisions.rationale: Render the assigned amount naturally while retaining the prohibition of excess.
key_decisions.before: He told them, “Collect no more than what has been assigned to you.”
key_decisions.after: He told them, “Collect no more than you have been authorized to collect.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Collect no more than what has been appointed for you.”

key_decisions.rationale: Retain coercion and false accusation as abuses and pay as the positive instruction without identifying the army.
key_decisions.before: Soldiers also asked him, “And what should we do?” He told them, “Do not extort money from anyone or make false accusations. Be content with your wages.”
key_decisions.after: Soldiers also asked, “And what should we do?” He said, “Do not extort money or accuse anyone falsely. Be content with your pay.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And soldiers also asked him, saying, “And we, what shall we do?” And he said to them, “Extort nothing from anyone, and accuse no one falsely, and be content with your wages.”

key_decisions.rationale: Retain all as the audience, comparative power, sandal service, and the paired Spirit/fire baptism.
key_decisions.before: John answered them all, “I baptize you with water, but one stronger than I am is coming. I am not worthy to untie the strap of his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
key_decisions.after: John answered them all, “I baptize you with water. But someone stronger than I is coming, and I am not worthy to untie his sandal strap. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: John answered, saying to all, “I baptize you with water, but the one more powerful than I is coming, the strap of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserve the complete agricultural image, separation, and unquenchable burning with a vocabulary aid.
key_decisions.before: His winnowing fork is in his hand to clear his threshing floor and gather the wheat into his barn, but he will burn the chaff with unquenchable fire.”
key_decisions.after: His winnowing fork is in his hand, ready to clear his threshing floor and gather the wheat into his storehouse. But he will burn the chaff with fire that cannot be put out.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: His winnowing fork is in his hand, to clear his threshing floor and to gather the wheat into his barn; but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire.”

key_decisions.rationale: Use an active construction to make the rebuker clear, without adding the brother's name absent here.
key_decisions.before: But Herod the tetrarch, after being confronted by John concerning Herodias, his brother’s wife, and all the evil things Herod had done,
key_decisions.after: But John rebuked Herod the tetrarch over Herodias, his brother's wife, and over all the evil Herod had done.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him concerning Herodias, his brother’s wife, and concerning all the evil things that Herod had done,

key_decisions.rationale: Retain the baptism among the people and prayer as the setting of the opening without naming an unstated baptizer.
key_decisions.before: When all the people had been baptized, Jesus was also baptized. As he was praying, heaven was opened,
key_decisions.after: When all the people were baptized, Jesus was baptized too. As he prayed, heaven opened,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Now when all the people were baptized, and when Jesus also had been baptized and was praying, heaven was opened,

key_decisions.rationale: Keep bodily form, the dove comparison, direct second-person address, and divine delight.
key_decisions.before: and the Holy Spirit descended on him in bodily form like a dove. A voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son; in you I am well pleased.”
key_decisions.after: and the Holy Spirit descended upon him in bodily form like a dove. A voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son; in you I take delight.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: and the Holy Spirit descended upon him in bodily form like a dove, and a voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son; in you I am well pleased.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserve approximate age, make the elliptical beginning intelligible as his work, and retain the qualification of Joseph's fatherhood before the ancestral chain.
key_decisions.before: Jesus himself was about thirty years old when he began his work. He was, as people supposed, son of Joseph, of Heli,
key_decisions.after: Jesus was about thirty years old when he began his work. He was, as people supposed, the son of Joseph, son of Heli,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And Jesus himself, when he began, was about thirty years old, being son, as was supposed, of Joseph, of Heli,

key_decisions.rationale: Use Joshua as the conventional English name for the Greek Iēsous in this ancestral position; retain all five names.
key_decisions.before: of Joshua, of Eliezer, of Jorim, of Matthat, of Levi,
key_decisions.after: son of Joshua, son of Eliezer, son of Jorim, son of Matthat, son of Levi,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: of Joshua, of Eliezer, of Jorim, of Matthat, of Levi,

key_decisions.rationale: Transliterate the pinned Jobel and Sala forms without silently replacing them from parallel genealogies.
key_decisions.before: of Jesse, of Obed, of Boaz, of Sala, of Nahshon,
key_decisions.after: son of Jesse, son of Jobel, son of Boaz, son of Sala, son of Nahshon,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: of Jesse, of Obed, of Boaz, of Sala, of Nahshon,

key_decisions.rationale: Preserve all six names, including both Admin and Arni, as this exact source gives them.
key_decisions.before: of Amminadab, of Admin, of Arni, of Hezron, of Perez, of Judah,
key_decisions.after: son of Amminadab, son of Admin, son of Arni, son of Hezron, son of Perez, son of Judah,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: of Amminadab, of Admin, of Arni, of Hezron, of Perez, of Judah,

key_decisions.rationale: Retain the ancestor spelled Kainam in Greek, conventionally Cainan in English, without removing a link to match a Hebrew genealogy.
key_decisions.before: of Cainan, of Arphaxad, of Shem, of Noah, of Lamech,
key_decisions.after: son of Cainan, son of Arphaxad, son of Shem, son of Noah, son of Lamech,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: of Cainan, of Arphaxad, of Shem, of Noah, of Lamech,

key_decisions.rationale: Preserve the second Cainan in its distinct position and the full five-name chain.
key_decisions.before: of Methuselah, of Enoch, of Jared, of Mahalaleel, of Cainan,
key_decisions.after: son of Methuselah, son of Enoch, son of Jared, son of Mahalaleel, son of Cainan,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: of Methuselah, of Enoch, of Jared, of Mahalaleel, of Cainan,

key_decisions.rationale: Keep the final four links and God as the genealogy's endpoint without adding a biological explanation.
key_decisions.before: of Enos, of Seth, of Adam, of God.
key_decisions.after: son of Enosh, son of Seth, son of Adam, son of God.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: of Enos, of Seth, of Adam, of God.
